chunks: Darkness is disappearing gradually, as though the travellers have arrived;

the hasteners will soon meet. Know, O my child, that everyone who is riding on the carriage of night and day is being carried by them even though he may be stationary, and he is covering the distance even though he is staying and resting.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of 'night and day' as a carriage in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this instruction to his son Hasan following the Battle of Siffin, Imam Hasan employs the metaphor of a mount to illustrate that time relentlessly transports the soul toward its destination, regardless of physical stillness or motion. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *zuhd* (asceticism) and the inevitability of *al-mawt* (death) as a journey where spiritual readiness matters more than worldly activity. The advice underscores the urgency of self-accountability (*muhasabah*) before the final return to the Creator.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Darkness is disappearing gradually. Now it is as though travellers have got down

and the hasteners will soon meet. Know, O my child, that everyone who is riding on the carriage of night and day is being carried by them even though he may be stationary, and he is covering the distance even though he is staying and resting.
